hints.title: Two-Child Removal Obstacle
hints.text: When deleting a node with two children, simply removing it breaks the tree structure. How can replacing the target with its in-order successor or predecessor preserve the ordering invariants?

hints.title: Successor Replacement Invariant
hints.text: If the node has at most one child, replace it with that child. If it has two children, replace its value with the minimum value in its right subtree, then recursively delete that minimum node.

hints.title: Recursive Case Analysis Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return null. If key < root.val, recurse left. If key > root.val, recurse right. If key matches: if left is null, return right; if right is null, return left. Otherwise find the minimum node in right subtree, set root.val to that minimum value, and recurse to delete that value from root.right.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: H: height of BST (log N balanced, N skewed)
complexity.notes: Recursive descent to find and delete target node with successor replacement in O(H) call stack.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Arbitrary splicing of subtrees violates the BST property or increases tree height uncontrollably.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly addressing three cases: no child, one child, and two children via successor.
